# Kurt

> Kurt is a small proof language with an automatic checker, for students learning to write
> mathematical proofs. A proof is a text file (`.kurt`) of claims, one per line, with indented
> blocks (`assume`, `let`, `pick`, `case`, `proof`); Kurt checks each line and prints why it
> holds. The implementation is one dependency-free Python file, `src/kurt/kurt.py`.

Writing Kurt proofs, the essentials:

- Declare symbols first: `bool A, B` (propositions), `const a, b`, `arity f 1`. Variables of
  rules start with `$` (objects) or `%` (propositions).
- Load theories: `load prop` (propositional logic), `logic` (quantifiers), `equality`, `set`,
  `numbers`, `natural` (induction), `analysis`, `group`, `modal`.
- `use F "label"` states an axiom; `show F` / `proof` / (indented steps) / `qed` proves a claim;
  a plain line `F` is a claim that must follow in one step from what is there.
- `assume A` opens a block; its last line `B` gives `A implies B` when the block closes by
  dedenting. `let x` gives `forall x ...`, `pick c with P c` uses `exists`.
- Check a file with `kurt FILE.kurt` (or `python -m kurt FILE.kurt`); `kurt --strict` rejects
  axioms and `todo` outside Kurt's own theories.

Website: https://www.kurt-lang.org (the playground, Kurt in the browser); repository: https://github.com/harmeling/kurt-lang
